subject: Export-control policy, technology migration and the distinction between installed memory-fab capacity and future effective bit supply

supported.finding: SK hynix's Wuxi source establishes an operating DRAM production line and states that technology scaling increased process count and equipment size enough to require additional cleanroom space; Samsung's Xi'an source independently establishes an operating NAND/V-NAND fabrication site.
supported.meaning: Installed fabs are real productive assets, but technology migration is not a purely software or naming change; it can require additional physical equipment and fab-space capability.

supported.finding: BIS's October 2022 policy text established new licensing requirements for PRC semiconductor-fab items at explicit advanced-memory thresholds, including DRAM at 18nm half-pitch or less and NAND at 128 layers or more.
supported.meaning: Equipment access for advanced memory production became a policy-conditioned variable distinct from installed nameplate fab existence.

supported.finding: BIS's October 2023 policy state identified Samsung and SK hynix PRC facilities as Validated End-Users and described a general-authorization mechanism for eligible items, explicitly framed as allowing continued PRC operations.
supported.meaning: The 2022 control regime did not imply a single permanent binary 'blocked' state; authorization pathways themselves changed over time and must be replayed by vintage.

supported.finding: BIS's August 2025 post-VEU policy explicitly separated intended licensing for operation of existing fabs from its stated intent not to grant licenses for capacity expansion or technology upgrades.
supported.meaning: Current fab operation and future migration/expansion capability are separable policy states. This is the strongest source-grounded support for MS-0115's core mechanism, but it is later-known and unavailable to 2022-2024 replay.

not_established: The packet does not establish that a particular Samsung or SK hynix equipment shipment was denied under the 2022 rule.
The packet does not quantify lost wafer starts, utilization, yield, DRAM bits, NAND bits or supplier revenue attributable to export controls.
The packet does not establish the 2022-2025 technology node or NAND layer count actually running at Wuxi or Xi'an.
The packet does not establish a quantitative mapping from licensing status to future bit-supply growth.
The packet does not yet cover YMTC or CXMT, so it must not generalize foreign-owned PRC-fab authorization mechanics to domestic Chinese memory producers.
The 2025 licensing-intent language is a later policy state and must not be used to reinterpret what a 2023 researcher could have known.

point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2022_10: A researcher can know that advanced PRC DRAM/NAND fab equipment access has entered a memory-specific licensing regime, but cannot know from this packet whether named foreign-owned fabs will lose operating continuity or future upgrade access.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2023_10: A researcher can additionally know that Samsung and SK hynix PRC facilities have a VEU/general-authorization pathway intended to support continued operations. The correct state is not simply 'export controls block China memory fabs'.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2024_12_31: The 2023 VEU authorization remains the latest grounded policy vintage in this packet. The 2025 revocation and explicit no-upgrade/no-expansion policy must remain hidden.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2025_08_30: A later researcher can know the policy regime changed again: continued existing-fab operation and future capacity/technology upgrades are explicitly separated.

assessment.representation_decision: Keep operating-fab state, physical technology-migration requirements, regulatory thresholds, authorization mechanism and later licensing intent as separate Evidence-level claims with independent known times. Treat any numerical future-bit-supply consequence as a distinct research/model layer unless directly measured by an authoritative source.
assessment.canonical_projection_decision: Do not add a new canonical Reality predicate for policy authorization in this single case. The existing Reality owner remains appropriate for measured industrial facts, but policy_text needs a stable reusable predicate design only after another real cross-industry policy trajectory demonstrates the same representation requirement.
assessment.outcome_for_ms0115: The core mechanism is supported qualitatively and temporally: installed capacity can continue to exist while the policy state governing future expansion or technology migration changes. The magnitude of the resulting future DRAM/NAND bit-supply constraint remains unresolved.

stop_rule.closed_surface: Do not turn generic export-control headlines into memory-supply numbers and do not repeatedly search the same Samsung/SK hynix VEU story without a new measurement or policy vintage.
reopen_when: A company primary source quantifies the technology, capacity, equipment or output effect at a named PRC memory fab.
BIS or another authoritative regulator publishes a materially new policy vintage affecting these memory fabs.
A second cross-industry policy trajectory demonstrates a reusable need for typed policy-state projection in the semantic catalog.
Methodological-primary market research measures the effect on DRAM/NAND wafer or bit supply with explicit methodology.

next_research_direction.principle: Prefer a high-importance sealed lead that tests a different methodology rather than another adjacent AI or export-control narrative.
next_research_direction.rationale: MS-0118 is a counterfactual lead around the 2017 memory upcycle—supplier discipline versus technology-transition supply constraints and demand-mix surprise—and would exercise Longcycle's ability to preserve competing causal explanations instead of selecting a hindsight narrative.
